columns.name: state
columns.description: This data element identifies the State in which the crash occurred. The codes are from the General Services Administration’s (GSA) publication of worldwide Geographic Location Codes (GLC).

columns.name: statename
columns.description: Source label for STATE. This data element identifies the State in which the crash occurred. The codes are from the General Services Administration’s (GSA) publication of worldwide Geographic Location Codes (GLC).

columns.name: st_case
columns.description: This data element is the unique case number assigned to each crash. It appears on each data file and is used to merge information from the data files together.

columns.name: peds
columns.description: This data element is the number of Person Forms (Not a Motor Vehicle Occupant) that are applicable to this case (i.e., non-occupants).

columns.name: pernotmvit
columns.description: This data element is a count of the number of non-motorists in the crash. A non-motorist is defined as a pedestrian, a cyclist, an occupant of a motor vehicle not in-transport, a person riding a horse, an occupant of an animal drawn conveyance, person associated with non-motorist conveyance (e.g., baby carriage, skateboard, wheelchair), or an other non-motorist (e.g., person outside a trafficway, person in a house).

columns.name: ve_total
columns.description: This data element is the number of contact motor vehicles that the officer reported on the police crash report as a unit involved in the crash.

columns.name: ve_forms
columns.description: This data element is a count of the number of motor vehicles in-transport involved in the crash. Legally parked vehicles are not included.

columns.name: pvh_invl
columns.description: This data element is a count of the number of parked and working vehicles involved in the crash.

columns.name: persons
columns.description: This data element is a count of the number of Person Level (Motor Vehicle Occupant) Forms that are applicable to this case (i.e., occupants).

columns.name: permvit
columns.description: This data element is a count of the number of motorists in the crash. A motorist is a driver, passenger, or unknown occupant type of a motor vehicle in-transport.

columns.name: county
columns.description: This data element records the location of the unstabilized event with regard to the County. The codes are from the General Services Administration’s (GSA) publication of worldwide Geographic Location Codes (GLC).

columns.name: countyname

columns.name: city

columns.name: cityname
columns.description: Source label for CITY. This data element records the location of the unstabilized event with regard to the City. The codes are from the General Services Administration’s (GSA) publication of worldwide Geographic Location Codes (GLC).

columns.name: month

columns.name: tway_id2

columns.name: route

columns.name: rur_urb

columns.name: rur_urbname
columns.description: Source label for RUR_URB. This data element identifies the classification of the segment of the trafficway on which the crash occurred based on FHWA-approved adjusted Census boundaries of small urban and urbanized areas.

columns.name: func_sysname
columns.description: Source label for FUNC_SYS. This data element identifies the functional classification of the segment of the trafficway on which the crash occurred.

columns.name: rd_owner
columns.description: This data element identifies the entity that has legal ownership of the segment of the trafficway on which the crash occurred. The entity that maintains the trafficway may differ from the owner in some locations.

columns.name: rd_ownername
columns.description: Source label for RD_OWNER. This data element identifies the entity that has legal ownership of the segment of the trafficway on which the crash occurred. The entity that maintains the trafficway may differ from the owner in some locations.

columns.name: nhs

columns.name: nhsname
columns.description: Source label for NHS. This data element identifies whether this crash occurred on a trafficway that is part of the National Highway System.

columns.name: sp_jur
columns.description: This data element identifies if the location on the trafficway where the crash occurred qualifies as a Special Jurisdiction even though it may be patrolled by State, county or local police (e.g., all State highways running through Indian Reservations are under the jurisdiction of the Indian Reservation).

columns.name: mileptname
columns.description: Source label for MILEPT. This data element records the milepoint nearest to the location where the crash occurred.

columns.name: longitud

columns.name: harm_ev

columns.name: man_coll
columns.description: This data element describes the orientation of two motor vehicles in-transport when they are involved in the “First Harmful Event” of a collision crash. If the “First Harmful Event” is not a collision between two motor vehicles in-transport, it is classified as such.

columns.name: reljct1
columns.description: This data element identifies the crash’s location with respect to presence in an interchange area. The coding of this data element is done in two sub-fields (see also C20B) and is based on the location of the “First Harmful Event” of the crash.

columns.name: reljct1name

columns.name: reljct2
columns.description: This data element identifies the crash’s location with respect to presence in or proximity to components typically in junction or interchange areas. The coding of this data element is done in two sub-fields (see also C20A) and is based on the location of the “First Harmful Event” of the crash.

columns.name: reljct2name

columns.name: rel_road

columns.name: wrk_zone
columns.description: This data element identifies a motor vehicle traffic crash in which the first harmful event occurs within the boundaries of a work zone or on an approach to or exit from a work zone, resulting from an activity, behavior, or control related to the movement of the traffic units through the work zone.

columns.name: hit_run

Hit-and-run is coded when a motor vehicle in-transport or its driver departs from the scene; vehicles not in-transport are excluded. It does not matter whether the hit-and-run vehicle was striking or struck.
